attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a Kea DHCP server on the private shared network (eth1/10.50.50.0/24, gateway .254, pool .100-.200, scoped via `listen-interface eth1` so it doesn't compete with the platform's default-network DHCP on eth0). node2 and node3 (RHEL10) already had ipv4.method=auto on their enp8s0 NICs facing this network; brought the connections up and both leased addresses from node1 (10.50.50.100 and 10.50.50.101 respectively), confirmed via node1's Kea lease table and bidirectional ping. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, verifying changed boot_id and post-restart recovery (DHCP service active + persisted leases on node1; reacquired DHCP addresses on node2/node3) each time.
